newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-REIFFEL ON TARGET FOR AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-REIFFEL ON TARGET FOR AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Seamer Paul Reiffel picked up three wickets against Leicestershire on Sunday as Australia's preparation for the second test against England was hit by rain.
Reiffel, who joined the Australian touring party last week as a replacement for the injured Andy Bichel, took three for 12 from 10 overs on day when only 30 overs were possible due to bad weather.
The Victorian was surprisingly overlooked by selectors for the six-test series despite taking 19 wickets in three tests on Australia's last tour of England in 1993.
Since joining the squad he has picked up six wickets for just 27 runs in 20 overs.
Australia captain Mark Taylor closed his side's innings at their overnight 220 for eight in a bid to give his bowling attack some practice ahead of the Lord's test which starts on Thursday.
Leicestershire slumped to 62 for four on the second day of the three-day match with leg-spinner Shane Warne also picking up a wicket.
Coach Geoff Marsh said Australia would be mentally ready for the second test despite the rain interruptions over the past week.
Last week the tourists lost one and a half day's play against Nottinghamshire and they have had little time on the field in their current game.
"It's unfortunate that we have lost so much time (here) and at Nottingham but this game is mostly played in the mind," Marsh said. "We will be all right for Lord's."
Reiffel is likely to be drafted into Australia's test team in place of Jason Gillespie, who has a hamstring injury.
